indicators.note: arrangements of a word's letters means the letters of alternative are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone weighing up other ways to organise a holiday or pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangements' signals the anagram: ALTERNATIVE's eleven letters are reordered. A tea interval is the break for tea in a British cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause for refreshments in a match or working day is a kind of rest, so the phrase means a break.

parts.note: reads like a quilt or blanket on a bed for sleeping, but the bed is a garden bed and the cover is its upper layer of earth

explanation.definitionFit: The uppermost layer of soil covers a flower bed or field, as a quilt covers a sleeper.

clue.text: A high range perceptible to the ear

parts.note: the Urals are a lofty mountain range dividing Europe from Asia

explanation.surface: A high band of sound frequencies that the human ear can just detect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A high range' suggests musical pitch, but the range is the Ural mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Something auditory is sensed through hearing, the faculty belonging to the ear.

indicators.note: the answer is made from the letters of Minnesota, rearranged, so from signals an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone who comes from the state of Minnesota puts forward a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals an anagram of MINNESOTA; 'someone' is a link that dresses the surface as a person's origin.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a candidate forward for office is to name them as a choice, which is proposing them.

definitions.meaning: colloquial slang for grub or a meal, informal and everyday
the verb: takes in food by gulping, consumes

explanation.surface: Asking what the birds called swallows usually feed on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' wants to be the birds; it is the verb meaning consumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal grub is called by this slang noun, and someone who swallows a meal consumes it.

indicators.note: the girl's name takes in, or holds, the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: Verity is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman considers how honest someone has been.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes account of' reads as one phrase meaning considers, but 'takes' is the container signal and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Honesty and accuracy of statement is the quality of telling the truth, which is truthfulness.

parts.note: reads as a dance that is banned, but the dance is performed by leaning back under a horizontal bar

explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean dance has performers bend backwards beneath a pole, which is literally a dance with a bar.

parts.note: formic acid is the chemical found in ants, so a formic solution playfully splits as an insect plus an acid, while the real remedy neutralises stomach acid

explanation.definitionFit: A stomach remedy that neutralises acid is taken to relieve indigestion.

indicators.note: the word for safe goes in the word for vile

parts.note: base means morally low or vile
a till is the cash drawer where a shop keeps money safe

explanation.surface: A strongbox kept inside a horrible stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' looks like an adjective; it is a noun, the shop's cash drawer. The Bastille was the Paris fortress-prison stormed in 1789.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was a medieval stronghold in Paris, used as a state prison.

clue.text: Peter frost enters within the boundary

indicators.note: the word for frost goes inside the name, entering within it

parts.note: taken as written, the man's name
rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: A man called Peter Frost walks onto a property's edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter frost' reads like a full name, but the surname is the icy coating, and 'enters within' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer edge or perimeter line enclosing an area is its boundary.

clue.text: An average sort of shirt is indicated

parts.note: the mean is a kind of average
a T-shirt is one kind of shirt

explanation.surface: Someone saying an ordinary shirt has been pointed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of shirt' gives T, as in T-shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: What was intended or signified by a word or sign is what it indicated.

clue.text: Overweight blondes, initially, yearn to get in shape

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of Overweight and of blondes

parts.note: to long for is to yearn

explanation.surface: Heavy fair-haired people wish to become fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in shape' looks like fitness, but 'shape' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle longer than it is wide is a geometric figure, a shape.

indicators.note: a kind or variant of the word Socratic, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Clever verbal games of the sort the philosopher Socrates enjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind' signals an anagram of SOCRATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A poem whose line initials spell a word is a form of verbal game or puzzle.

parts.note: the grid entries in a crossword have a technical name

explanation.definitionFit: Crossword entries are called by this term, and the English legal phrase for a long-standing right to daylight prefixes it with ancient.

clue.text: Well-mannered class setting socially acceptable standards

parts.note: a well-behaved child is good
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: A polite school year sets the bar for proper behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper etiquette is behaviour that matches accepted conventions of manners.

clue.text: Surprised to find the vehicle is carrying acid

indicators.note: the vehicle carries the word for acid inside it

parts.note: a sled is a vehicle on runners
tart means sharp or acid in taste

explanation.surface: Shock at discovering a car is transporting corrosive chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acid' looks like a corrosive chemical the vehicle is hauling; it is an adjective meaning sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given a sudden fright or shock means being surprised.

clue.text: Contest in which no one goes the distance

definitions.text: Contest in which no one goes the distance

parts.words: Contest in which no one goes the distance
parts.note: sounds like a race everyone abandons, but each runner covers only one leg of a team event

explanation.definitionFit: In a team running event each member runs one stage, so no single runner covers the full course.

clue.text: Use a stop-over — a humble dwelling

parts.note: to bung a hole is to put a stopper over it
low means humble or lowly

explanation.surface: Advice to break a journey at a modest little house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stop-over' looks like a break in travel; it is a stopper over a hole, which is to bung it.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-storey house is a type of home, a dwelling.

clue.text: Saw, perhaps, but angry and pretended not to see

parts.note: cross means angry
to cut someone is to snub them, pretending not to see them

explanation.surface: Someone noticed a person yet, annoyed, acted as if they had not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see; it is the tool. A crosscut saw cuts across the grain.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosscut is a type of saw made for cutting wood across the grain, so a saw is an example.

definitions.meaning: British slang for clothes and gear

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a garment factory's workers will down tools.
explanation.walkthrough: The British slang noun means one's gear or clothes; the verb means to hit hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang noun covers one's outfit and belongings, and the verb means to batter or hit.

parts.note: suggests a pensioner doing nothing, but retirement here means retiring to bed for the night

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has retired to bed at night lies at rest, dozing.

clue.text: I'd enter uphill events alongside a motor-bike

indicators.note: the letters of I'd go into the reversed word
in a down clue uphill means the word races is read from the bottom up

parts.note: races are sporting events
the contraction I'd, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone enters hill-climb contests next to a motorcycle.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uphill' reverses the events, giving SECAR, which the contraction enters. The definition describes the vehicle by where it rides: beside a motor-bike.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger car attached at the side of a motorcycle sits beside it.

parts.note: an event called off is cancelled
a stage is a stagecoach

explanation.surface: An actor idle because the tour bus has been cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coach' looks like a bus or trainer; it is a stage, short for stagecoach.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor out of view of the audience in the wings is not performing.

clue.text: It may be held up or down

indicators.note: in a down entry the word reads the same whether read upwards or downwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Something that can be raised or lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up or down' says the answer reads the same both ways in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle or belief is something a person holds.

parts.note: suggests a camera part, but the shutter is the flap of skin that closes over the eye

explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin that closes over the eye acts like a shutter on a window.

parts.note: a leg is a limb or member of the body
L is for learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A member of an institution who is studying law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' looks like a club member; it is a limb. L is the learner plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the justice system and its rules means concerning law.

definitions.meaning: a projecting knob or boss that stands out from a surface
a farm or establishment where horses are bred

explanation.surface: A superb manager is right for the horse-yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding boss' looks like a great manager; it is a raised knob standing out from a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised knob standing proud of a surface is a boss, and a horse-breeding establishment is also so called.

clue.text: Poet possibly born around the end of the century

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the picked letter
possibly signals the letters of born may be rearranged
the end of means take the last letter of century

explanation.surface: A poet who was perhaps born near the close of the century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns BORN into BRON, and 'around' puts it round Y, picked by 'the end of' from century. 'Poet possibly' looks like a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Byron was a famous English Romantic writer of verse.

indicators.note: the letters of teach girl are put into a new form

explanation.surface: Instruct a young woman while she is sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' signals an anagram of TEACH GIRL; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggish and lacking energy, as a lethargic person is, means torpid.

clue.text: He spends most of his time out of the country

definitions.text: He spends most of his time out of the country

parts.words: He spends most of his time out of the country
parts.note: suggests an expatriate living abroad, but the country is the countryside as opposed to the city

explanation.definitionFit: A city resident lives in an urban area rather than the rural countryside.
